Poramati: A tale from 1971
2014-12-17T00:00:54+06:00 | Saurav Dey
https://www.thedailystar.net/poramati-a-tale-from-1971-55669

Padatik Natya Sangsad Bangladesh premiered their 31st production “Poramati” at the Experimental Theatre Hall of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy on December 14 evening.

Written by Babul Biswas, the play — a narrative from a torture camp of Pakistani Military during the Liberation War — has been directed by Dr. Irin Pervin Lopa. Selim SH Chowdhury, Team Leader of Padatik, is the art director of the play.

The play depicts an earthy tale of sheer horror narrated by a number of prisoners held by the Pakistani Army. The perpetrators insinuate the poison of betrayal into the prisoners and it leads to a crack in their unity. Betrayal poisons the mind of Bangladeshis during the war shattering their unity, and the play brings forth that tale of betrayal and killing by the Pakistani Military and their local collaborators.

“Poramati” fits well into the present socio-political context where people are running after personal interest instead of collective welfare of the society.

Omiyo Mizan, Kamruzzaman Pavel, Al Amin, Faruk Faysal Duke, Mahmuda Akter Lita and Kamal Hossain played different roles in the play. One of the strongest aspects of the play was the bold, near-perfect acting. What was even more commending was that three members of the cast were debutants on stage.

Three members of Martyred Intellectuals families -- Panna Kaiser, Shyamoli Nasrin Chowdhury and Zaheed Reza Noor attended the premiere, along with Indian Deputy High Commissioner Sandip Chakraborty.

A realistic set design coupled with vivid imagery, and an audio-visual in the background gave the audience a glimpse of what happened in 1971. The representation on stage was so vivid that Syamoli Nasrin Chowdhury and Panna Kaiser had a hard time sitting through it. The play deserves applause, though one and half hour runtime seemed tad lengthy for this compact narrative.
